problems.title: Resolve these problems before publishing
problems.remainder_count: At most one target may take the remainder.
problems.fixed_percent_missing: Every non-remainder target needs a fixed percent.
problems.fixed_percent_sum: Fixed percents must total 100 or name a remainder target.
problems.effective_window: The effective window is inverted or missing.
problems.effective_overlap: The effective window overlaps another published version.
problems.book_scope: The book scope names no usable posting book.
problems.apply_policy: Entry rules need a line behavior.
problems.targets_empty: At least one target is required.
problems.source_measure: Period sweeps need a source measure.
problems.target_sequence: Targets must be ordered without gaps.
problems.dynamic_min_weight: The minimum weight must be zero or more.
problems.driver_missing: A driver basis needs a driver.
problems.driver_unknown: The driver does not exist in this organization.
problems.driver_dimension: The driver measures a different dimension.
problems.stepped_tiers: A stepped basis needs at least one tier.
problems.offset_impact: An offset account only coheres with reclassify impact.
problems.residual_target: The explicit residual target is missing or unknown.
problems.fallback: This version cannot be published yet.

when.title: When should this fire?
when.description: Same rule model, three moments. Pick the one that matches when the split should happen.

entry.title: When a line is entered
entry.description: Saving a matching bill, expense, or journal line replaces it with the split children.
entry.example: A 1,000.00 overhead bill becomes four department lines at a 1 : 2 : 3 : 4 ratio.

period.title: At month-end
period.description: A period sweep reads a pool, apportions it, and posts its own allocation journal.
period.example: Untagged IT spend is reclassed onto every department by headcount after the period closes.

post.title: When the document posts
post.description: Extra journal lines land on the same entry, stamped with this rule as the contributor.
post.example: Use this when the source document should stay whole and the allocation is GL-only.

source.title: Which lines should it catch?
source.description: Name the rule, then filter by transaction type and any matcher dimension. Empty transaction types mean every kind.
source.kindsHint: These are document kinds. Leave them all off to match every type.
source.anyKind: Nothing selected means every transaction type.
source.filtersHint: AND-ed with the transaction types. Leave a dimension on Any to ignore it. Period sweeps often collect the untagged pool.
source.filtersAny: Every dimension starts at Any. Switch to These only for the classifiers that should constrain the match.
source.noValues: No active values for this dimension yet.

split.title: How should the amount split?
split.description: A fixed ratio is a named split (1, 2, 3, 4). A driver is a reusable measure you attach here — drivers are not rules.

ratio.title: Fixed ratio
ratio.description: Relative weights such as 1 : 2 : 3 : 4. Stored as percents that always sum to 100.
ratio.example: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10 parts, so the shares are 10%, 20%, 30%, and 40%.

percent.title: Fixed percent
percent.description: Type the percents yourself. They must total 100.

driver.title: Existing driver
driver.description: Headcount, hours, a manual table, or a saved report. Create the driver on the Drivers tab, then pick it here.

split.driverEmpty: No drivers yet. A fixed ratio does not need one. Create a driver only when the weights should change each period.
split.driverHint: The driver measures one dimension. Dynamic targets follow that dimension at run time.

targets.title: Where does the money go?
targets.description: Pick the destination dimension and give each value a share. Empty account keeps the source account.
targets.noValues: No active values for that dimension yet.
targets.needOne: Pick at least two destinations with a positive share.
targets.driverDynamic: {driver} will split across every {dimension} that has weight.
targets.driverDynamicHint: No need to list destinations — the driver vector is the target set.

policy.title: What should the books do?
policy.description: Whether the split is automatic, and whether cost moves or only dimensional attribution is added.
policy.applySuggestHint: The line grid offers a chip; the split applies on click.
policy.applyManualHint: The split only appears in the line's distribution picker.
policy.impactReclassHint: Credit the source coordinate and debit each target. Trial balance total holds.
policy.impactNetZeroHint: Net-zero pair: company profit does not change; dimensions do.
policy.periodActivityHint: Allocate this period's posted activity, excluding this rule's own lines.
policy.periodBalanceHint: Allocate the period-end balance of the source pool.
policy.runManualHint: You preview and post from the Runs tab.
policy.runAutoPreviewHint: After period end, compute a preview automatically. You still post it.

review.title: Create this rule?
review.description: This writes the same versioned rule the drawer edits. You can change anything after.

lineage.title: Allocation lineage
lineage.empty: No allocated lines trace to this record.
